title: add vpc control plane provisioning: subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, route53
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Add full VPC control plane provisioning module to support Private deployments (VPC/private installer) in multi-AZ accounts. This PR introduces Terraform modules and Helm chart tweaks to provision control-plane subnets, interface endpoints (S3, ECR, Secrets Manager, KMS), security groups with least-privilege rules, cross-account VPC peering for control plane connectivity, and Route53 private hosted zone automation. Includes upgrades to the installer hooks so upgrades/rollbacks reconcile endpoint and peering state safely. The change set is intended to be idempotent and follow existing Redwood networking conventions. Changes: - terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane: new module that creates subnets (public/isolated for control plane), route tables, NAT gateway attachments, interface endpoints, and security groups with explicit egress/ingress rules. - terraform/modules/vpc-peering: cross-account peering support with automated route propagation and tagging. - terraform/envs/*: example environment configs and variable mappings for multi-az deployments. - helm/redwood-private/values.yaml: optional flags to enable/disable automated route53 association and peering acceptance. - installer/upgrade-hooks: adds post-upgrade checks to validate endpoints and peering routes and safe rollback path. Testing and validation: - Local terraform plan/apply in a staging account with three AZs and cross-account peer accepted by automation. - Integration test harness (perf-canary) ran smoke checks verifying private Route53 resolution for control-plane hostnames and SSToken auth to S3 via endpoint. - Security review verified SG rules and KMS access boundaries. Migration and rollout notes: - Default behavior is opt-in via values.enableAutoNetworking=false so existing customers are not impacted. - For customers who opt-in, rollout should be canaried to a single account then rolled out across org units. Rollback: uninstall hook removes peering and endpoints only if created by module; otherwise marks resources as managed=false and logs instructions for manual reconciliation. Related: ENG-3124 (private deploy networking), OPS-88 (upgrade automation).

chore(terraform): add example envs and variables for multi-az deployment
feat(installer): installer upgrade hooks for endpoint/peering reconciliation
fix(helm): add flags for route53-association and peering-acceptance toggles
docs: add runbook and rollout steps for private control plane networking
changed_files: terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane/main.tf - new module creating aws_subnet, aws_route_table, aws_eip, aws_nat_gateway, aws_vpc_endpoint_interface, aws_security_group
terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane/outputs.tf - outputs for subnet ids, endpoint ids, peering ids
terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane/variables.tf - inputs for az mapping, cidr blocks, account ids
terraform/modules/vpc-peering/main.tf - cross-account aws_vpc_peering_connection, route propagation, acceptance automation
terraform/envs/staging/vars.tfvars - example multi-az variables used in testing
installer/upgrade-hooks/post_upgrade_check.sh - script to validate endpoints and routes after upgrade
installer/upgrade-hooks/rollback_plan.md - instructions and automation markers for safe rollback
tests/integration/vpc_control_plane_smoke_test.go - smoke tests for DNS, endpoints, and connectivity
review_comments: Evelyn Park: please add a note in the runbook about DNS TTLs and how changes can take up to 60s to propagate. Also verify that endpoints are created in each az to avoid cross-az charges.
Asha Patel: addressed: added TTL note and ensured aws_vpc_endpoint_interface is created per-az. Updated README with cost note.
Jonah Kim: security review: request explicit deny-egress rule be avoided to prevent blocking control plane egress for health checks. Also request KMS key policy scope review.
Asha Patel: removed restrictive deny-egress, added scoped IAM role assumption for peering acceptance, and attached KMS key policy used by control-plane service account only.
Liam O'Connor: CI saw intermittent terraform fmt failure on pipeline; please run fmt and re-run plan in CI.
Asha Patel: ran terraform fmt and pinned provider versions to reduce drift; pushed fix, re-ran pipeline.
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after 3 approvals and a successful staging apply. Opt-in feature behind helm flag to avoid surprise changes for existing customers.
release_notes: Added terraform module and installer hooks to automate VPC control-plane provisioning (subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 association). Opt-in via helm values.enableAutoNetworking. Runbook and rollback steps included.
testing_summary: Staging apply in multi-AZ account, integration smoke tests validated endpoint connectivity and private Route53 resolution, security review passed with minor policy adjustments.
manual_steps: To enable: set helm/redwood-private.values.enableAutoNetworking=true and provide peer_account_id and route53_hosted_zone_id. Follow runbook to canary in one account before org-wide rollout.
notes_for_ops: The module creates peering connections which will be auto-accepted if autoAcceptPeering=true and peering role permissions exist in the accepter account. If running cross-account, ensure the accepter has the peering IAM role configured or set autoAcceptPeering=false and accept manually.
regression_risks: Low when opt-in. If enabled across many accounts simultaneously, potential for transient DNS resolution issues during Route53 association changes and brief connectivity gaps during peering creation; use canary rollout.
